title: India Ends Mail-In OCI Applications in Canada, Mandates In-Person Biometrics
excerpt: All OCI applications in Canada must now be filed online and verified in person at BLS International centres, ending decades of postal submissions and introducing electronic OCI cards.
body:
• From April 5, 2026, all OCI applications in Canada must be submitted in person at designated BLS International centres, with postal applications permanently discontinued.
  • India's Citizenship (Amendment) Rules 2026 shift all OCI applications worldwide to a digital-only portal and introduce electronic OCI cards linked to a centralized verification registry.
  • A uniform global fee structure sets fresh applications at USD 275, with processing times expected to drop from six to eight weeks to 15 working days.
  • Minor children can no longer hold Indian and foreign passports simultaneously, forcing thousands of diaspora families to make earlier nationality decisions.

Postal Applications Permanently Ended

Indians in Canada can no longer mail in their Overseas Citizenship of India applications. Starting April 5, 2026, the Consulate General of India in Toronto and Vancouver and the High Commission in Ottawa require all OCI applications to be submitted in person at BLS International centres, where applicants must provide biometrics as part of the process.

The change eliminates a postal option that millions of diaspora families had relied on for years. The new rule applies to everyone — first-time applicants, renewals, and those converting Persons of Indian Origin cards to OCI status. There are no exceptions for distance or convenience.

BLS International, India's exclusive outsourced service provider in Canada, now serves as the mandatory gatekeeper for all OCI submissions. Applicants must book an appointment and appear in person for document verification, fee payment, and biometric capture. If paperwork is not in order at the counter, the application is rejected on the spot, requiring a fresh appointment.

Broader Overhaul Under New National Rules

The Canada-specific postal ban is part of a sweeping overhaul. India's Citizenship (Amendment) Rules 2026, notified through a Gazette notification on May 1, require all OCI applications worldwide — whether for registration, reissuance, renunciation, or updates — to be filed online through the official portal at ociservices.gov.in.

The old paper application process, where applicants submitted duplicate forms with hard-copy photos and signatures, has been permanently eliminated. While the initial application is now entirely portal-based, document verification at Indian missions and consulates still requires presenting originals in person.

The changes affect an estimated 5.5 million OCI cardholders worldwide, according to government figures. Processing times under the new digital system are expected to average 15 working days for straightforward cases, down from the previous six to eight weeks under the paper process.

Electronic OCI Cards and Real-Time Border Verification

The 2026 rules introduce electronic OCI, or e-OCI, under which registered individuals may receive either a physical card or an electronic credential recorded in a new standardized format called Form XXIX. Physical cards remain available on request but are no longer mandatory for travel or immigration clearance in India.

The e-OCI links to a centralized electronic registry that allows border officials and Indian missions to verify cardholder status in real time. By December 2026, the government plans to integrate this data with the Immigration, Visa and Foreigners Registration and Tracking platform, known as IVFRT 2.0, which already powers automated e-gates at 13 international airports across India.

Once integration is complete, e-OCI holders should be able to use facial-recognition lanes for faster entry and exit processing at equipped airports.

New Rules Hit Families With Minor Children

A provision added to Rule 3 of the Citizenship Rules explicitly bars any minor child from holding an Indian passport and a foreign passport at the same time. Parents applying for an Indian passport for a child must now sign a declaration confirming that no foreign passport will be obtained while the Indian passport remains active. Children who already hold a foreign passport must surrender it before a new Indian passport can be issued.

"The system has fundamentally changed from a remote process to a mandatory in-person one. If you don't show up, your application doesn't proceed."

— HelpOCI, immigration documentation service

The rule is expected to affect thousands of diaspora families in Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Gulf countries who have historically maintained both documents for their children while deciding on long-term nationality choices.

What OCI Holders Need to Know

India also introduced a uniform global fee structure in April. A fresh OCI application filed at any Indian mission abroad now costs USD 275, with Canadian applicants paying a total of CAD $376 plus a BLS processing fee of $1.70 and courier charges. Reissuance for a change of particulars or the mandatory update after turning 20 costs USD 25, while replacing a lost or damaged card costs USD 100.

OCI registration is now also liable for cancellation if a cardholder has been sentenced to imprisonment for two years or more, or has been formally charge-sheeted for an offence punishable by seven or more years — even before conviction. Cancellation can take effect electronically through the government's digital register, meaning a cardholder's legal status now rests in the portal record rather than the physical card.

Applicants now provide biometric consent at enrollment, feeding into India's Fast-Track Immigration Trusted Traveller Program and connecting OCI records to the country's Unique Identification ecosystem for additional identity verification at borders.

For OCI holders who recently renewed their Canadian passport, the critical step is ensuring their record on ociservices.gov.in reflects the current passport number. A mismatch between the passport on file and the passport presented at check-in is the most common reason for boarding refusals and secondary inspections at Indian immigration counters. Missing the three-month update window now triggers a mandatory USD 25 penalty under the revised fee structure. The rules are already in effect, and the penalties for non-compliance are automatic.

nri_angle: The new rules directly affect millions of Indian diaspora members worldwide, requiring all 5.5 million OCI cardholders to transition to a digital-first system and mandating in-person biometrics for applications in Canada.
